--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.relabel_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Rename nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.relabel_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Rename nodes. title: >- [Graph.relabel_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Rename nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Rename nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17226-L17335){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.relabel_nodes(mapping) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Relabel nodes](../assets/graphs/relabel-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph with each node's id in a pill, 1 to 6. The call renames B to X and E to Y; after it those two nodes carry their new labels in the accent color, while their ids 2 and 5, the edges, and the other labels are unchanged." width="100%"} Changes node labels in place, leaving node IDs, attributes and edges untouched. This is the tool for cleaning up names after import (fixing typos, normalizing case, swapping accession numbers for gene symbols) or for making labels match another dataset before a join. `mapping=` is either a dictionary from existing nodes (IDs or labels) to new labels, which renames only the nodes it mentions, or a function that receives each node's current label and returns its new one, applied to every node. Renames happen all at once, so labels can be swapped (`{"A": "B", "B": "A"}`). If the result would give two nodes the same label, nothing is changed and a `ValueError` is raised. Unlike NetworkX's `relabel_nodes()`, which builds new node keys, EdgeCase keeps each node's integer ID, so anything stored by ID (selections, results from `return_dict=True`) stays valid. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mapping]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[dict, Callable[[str], str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary mapping node IDs or labels to new labels, or a function from the current label to the new label. New labels must be strings. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph itself, for chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node in the mapping does not exist, or two nodes would end up with the same label. [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a new label is not a string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Rename a couple of nodes by label: ::: {#1f56db74 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["a", "b", "c"]) .add_edges([("a", "b"), ("b", "c")]) .relabel_nodes({"a": "alpha", "b": "beta"}) ) graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['alpha--beta', 'beta--c'] ``` ::: ::: A function renames every node at once: ::: {#e1747577 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.relabel_nodes(str.upper).get_node_df().select(["id", "label"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 2)
idlabel
i64str
1"ALPHA"
2"BETA"
3"C"
``` ::: ::: Swapping two labels works because all renames happen together: ::: {#c334c835 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.relabel_nodes({"ALPHA": "BETA", "BETA": "ALPHA"}).get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['BETA--ALPHA', 'ALPHA--C'] ``` ::: :::
